evidence.note: עוֹבָל appears by name alongside Abimael and Sheba.
The closing statement identifies all those listed as sons of Joktan.

article.name: עוֹבָל
article.summary: Obal is a son of Joktan. Genesis lists him immediately before Abimael and Sheba.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for עוֹבָל. Leave the root unassigned because the passage gives no support for the proposed meaning “spotted” or “marked.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:26 introduces Joktan as the father, 10:28 names Obal, and 10:29 calls those listed Joktan’s sons.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 10:28 names Obal alongside Abimael and Sheba, each introduced by וְאֶת. Genesis 10:29 identifies them all as sons of Joktan. The genealogy gives no explanation of the name’s meaning.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun without a prefix or suffix. The preceding וְאֶת is a separate word that marks Obal as another direct object of יָלַד, “fathered,” in Genesis 10:26.

evidence.note: Abimael appears between Obal and Sheba in the list identified in verse 29 as Joktan’s sons.
The parallel genealogy preserves the same name in the same position.
Isaac addresses Abraham as אָבִי, “my father,” illustrating the father element.

article.name: אֲבִימָאֵל
article.summary: Abimael is a son of Joktan. The opening אֲבִי corresponds to אָב, “father.” The meaning of the full name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Abimael, linked to אָב through the opening element אֲבִי.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:26–29 lists Abimael among Joktan’s sons. The parallel genealogy repeats his name between Obal and Sheba in 1 Chronicles 1:22.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 10:28 places אֲבִימָאֵל between Obal and Sheba. Each name follows וְאֶת as the list of Joktan’s sons continues from verse 26.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal proper noun referring to a male. The preceding וְאֶת is a separate word. The name has no attached prefix or suffix.
